headline: Computational pipelines integrate omics data to nominate cancer targets and niches
label: Multi Omics Biomarker Target Prioritization
summary: Integrative transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial workflows now nominate survival-linked cancer targets and communication axes.
synthesis: The common thread is a staged computational workflow for nominating molecular targets, in which transcriptomic, single-cell, or spatial data are integrated with differential expression, machine learning, and survival analysis. SKyNet extends this to ligand-receptor pairs prioritized against survival across pan-solid cancers, Harmonics applies hierarchical distribution matching to separate common and condition-specific spatial cell niches, and the M2 macrophage signature combines multi-omics data with machine learning for breast cancer prognosis. The SF3B1 study adds a long-read route, identifying mutation-linked lncRNAs that yield translatable peptides. Other items pair integrative analysis with experimental checks, including the colorectal liver metastasis signature and the SP1 Co-IP/MS study. Not all items fit this pattern: RAPPL-Seq is a ribosome profiling methods advance, and the glucocorticoid study addresses noncoding genome regulation.
